properties.NAME: (Agnes) Kittlesby Hall
properties.Information: Hilleboe and Kittelsby, which are connected by a common entrance, offer the largest triple rooms on campus, and house around 360 first-year and upper class students.

properties.NAME: (Agnes) Larson Hall
properties.Information: Larson Hall houses 307 students, including the college's international students. The circular arrangement of each floor in Larson creates a strong community atmosphere.

properties.NAME: (Agnes) Mellby Hall
properties.Information: Mellby Hall houses 190 students in a warm and comfortable atmosphere. Mellby is the oldest hall on campus and its historic appeal truly stands out. It features a kitchen, TV lounge, computer facilities, and a comfortable main lounge and fireplace.

properties.NAME: (Gertrude) Hillboe Hall
properties.Information: Hilleboe and Kittelsby, which are connected by a common entrance, offer the largest triple rooms on campus, and house around 360 first-year and upper class students.

properties.NAME: (Tweet) Hall of Music
properties.Information:
The Hall of Music, which opened in February 2012, provides extended space for the Music Department.

Complementing Christiansen Hall of Music, the new Hall of Music (more commonly known as the "Music Box") hosts 36 practice rooms, including two concerto rooms with two grand pianos; four chamber music rehearsal spaces; a reed room for double reeds; a percussion suite; 12 faculty studios; and the Music Department office.

The Hall of Music connects with Alumni Hall to the west and the Center for Art and Dance (home to the Art/Art History and Dance departments) to the east.

Related Links
  • Music Department

properties.NAME: Ade Christenson Complex
properties.Information:
The Ade Christenson Complex on the east side of campus is home to Klein Field at Manitou, the Manitou Track, and Tom Porter Hall.

The playing and running surfaces are first-class competition sites for the football and men's and women's track and field teams. Two classrooms, locker rooms, an athletic training room, offices for coaches and staff, and a weight room make Tom Porter Hall a convenient home to the football, track and field, and men's and women's hockey teams.

The lobby overlooks the west end zone and track, and it has a clear view of the bleachers and press box. The venue is also the home of the college's commencement ceremonies.

properties.NAME: Alumni Hall
properties.Information: Alumni Hall is home to the Advancement Divison, which includes the offices of Development, Annual Giving, Alumni and Parent Relations, Stewardship, and Advancement Services. Also house in the building are Marketing and Communication, College Events, and Music Orgnaizations, which provides support for the ensemble tours and Christmas Festival. As part of the Clemens V. Granskou Compex, named in the honor of the fifth president of St. Olaf College, Alumni Hall connects to the Hall of Music, which serves as an annex to Christiansen Hall of Music.

properties.NAME: Boe Memorial Chapel
properties.Information: Worship is the primary purposes of Boe Chapel, which houses the Office of College Ministrat. During daily chapel services the community hears from faculty members, students and campus guests. And each Sunday morning while school is in session, the Student Congregation gathers for worship. Student and faculty musicians offer the fits and talents, not just as soloists but as members of bands, choirs, orchestras, and small ensembles.

properties.NAME: Buntrock Commons
properties.Information:
With dining facilities, a bookstore, a post office, the Lion's Pause student club, and more, Buntrock Commons is the hub of campus. Learn more here.

properties.NAME: Center for Art and Dance
properties.Information:
In additional to housing classrooms, studios, and offices for the Art Department and Dance Department, the Center for Art and Dance is home to the Flaten Art Museum, which presents exhibits of renowned works and contains and extensive permanent collection of traditional and contemporary textiles, paintings, sculpture, ceramics, and works on paper.

  • Dance Department

properties.NAME: Christiansen Hall of Music
properties.Information:
Christiansen Hall of Music is a home of the Music Department and part of the Music Organizations staff that supports concerts and tours by the ensembles.

Named after St. Olaf choir founder F. Melius Christiansen, the building houses Urness Recital Hall, the Margaret Skoglund Reception Room, the Halvorson Music Library, three ensemble rehearsal rooms, classrooms, practice rooms, faculty studios, and the electronic music studio.

Related Links
  • Music Department
  • Christmas Festival

properties.NAME: Ellingson Hall
properties.Information: Ellingson Hall is located on the Northeast side of campus near Mohn and Thorson Halls. Ellingson Hall is a four story building housing 185 first-year students. With centralized lounge spaces on every floor, Ellingson Hall offers an intellectual atmosphere for students to easily meet, study and hangout outside of their rooms.

properties.NAME: Flaten Art Barn
properties.Information: The Flaten Art Barn, which opened fall 2013 in its new location adjacent to the wind turbine, is a reconstruction of a 1932 building that served as the first home of the college's Art Department. It is named after its designer/builder and the founder of what is now the Department of Art and Art History, Arnold Flaten.

properties.NAME: Holland Hall
properties.Information:
Holland Hall was dedicated in 1925 as part of the celebrations for the college's 50th anniversary. Architects for the building drew inspiration for the building's design from Mon-Saint-Michel, the fortress monastery on the coast of Normandy, France. In particular, they designed it to resemble the Merville - the monastery's assembly hall and dining area.

Although the power plant built in 1935 was the first building on campus to display the limestone-studded Norma Gothic style that has become the hallmark of the Hill, it wasn't until Holland Hall was built that the architectural style made its full impact.

Longtime faculty member Peter Olai Holland, who also served as the college's treasurer and director of finance, was St. Olaf President Lars W. Boe's "right-hand man".

Related Links
  • St. Olaf College News - November 1, 2017: The new Holland Hall

properties.NAME: Hoyme Hall
properties.Information: Hoyme Hall is a four-story hall housing 210 first-year students. The main lounge provides a striking view of the surrounding countryside as well as a wonderful space for studying and socializing. Students in the Great Conversation program live in Hoyme.

properties.NAME: Kildahl Hall
properties.Information: Kildahl Hall offers a friendly, comfortable atmosphere for 168 students. The main lounge serves as the center of community, offering many activities and late night conversations around the fireplace. Kildahl is equipped with lofted beds, computer facilities, and a strong community that is ideal for studying and socializing.

properties.NAME: Madson Facilities Building
properties.Information: The Norman E. Madson building houses the offices of the Facilities Department and the college's power plant.

properties.NAME: Mohn Hall
properties.Information: One of the two towers on campus, Mohn Hall is a ten-story residence hall housing 307 students. The hall, which traditionally houses first-year and upperclass students by floor, offers a main lounge, a recreational room, and a piano room. The circular arrangement of each corridor creates a strong community atmosphere.

properties.NAME: New Hall
properties.Information: New Hall offers 300 student beds with 30 single rooms (three accessible rooms) along with 135 double rooms. Learn more about the amenities and accommodations available

properties.NAME: Old Main
properties.Information:
Built in 1877, Old Main was the first - and originally the only - building to occupy Manitou Heights, containing classrooms, a library, housing for students and faculty, and a dining room.

Through the years, Old Main has housed various departments in the humanities and now is home to the Religion Department.

The hill to the east of the building is a popular sledding venue for students and local neighbors.

properties.NAME: Rand Hall
properties.Information: Rand Hall, nestled into the north face of Manitou Heights, houses 243 upper-class men and women. A variety of living options are available in Rand including single, double, and quad occupancy rooms. Suites share their own bathrooms. The hillside location offers a beautiful view of the woods and fields surrounding the college.

properties.NAME: Regents Hall of Mathematical Sciences
properties.Information:
This building was renovated as part of the same project that opened Regents Hall in 2008.

The building - along with the adjacent Regents Hall of Natural Sciences - has become an invaluable teaching tool for the nearly 40 percent of St. Olaf students who pursue a major or concentration in the natural sciences or mathematics.

properties.NAME: Regents Hall of Natural Sciences
properties.Information:
With such features as a green roof, aggressive daylighting, and the minimization of chemical and biological waste, LEED Platinum-certified Regents Hall is not simply a model for responsible environmental stewardship, but a daily working example of sustainability in practice.

Since opening in fall 2008, the building - along with the adjacent Regents Hall of Mathematical Sciences - has become an invaluable teaching tool for nearly 40 percent of St. Olaf students who pursue a major or concentration in the natural sciences or mathematics.

properties.NAME: Rolvaag Memorial Library
properties.Information:
Completed in 1942 and named in honor of 1905 alumnus Ole Rolvaag, former St. Olaf professor of Norwegian and author of Giants in the Earth, Rolvaag Library is the largest of three libraries on the St. Olaf campus (the others are the Hustad Science Library in Regents Hall and then Halvorson Music Library in Christiansen Hall of Music).

Special Collections and College Archives are located on the second floor of Rolvaag Memorial Library. The Halvorson Music Library is located in the Christiansen Hall of Music.

The fourth floor of Rolvaag is home to the Information Technology (IT) Department and the Digital Scholarship Center (DiSCO), which provides the campus community assistance with technology and digital scholarship.

The English Department and classrooms are located on the fifth floor of the library in the original section of the building.

properties.NAME: Skifter Hall
properties.Information:
Hector Skifter Hall houses the administrative offices for Broadcast Media and extended practice/studio space for the Music Department. Home to the college's organ studies, Skifter Hall has been specifically redesigned and renovated to house several practice organs and rehearsal spaces acoustically engineered for the instrument.

The Tormodsgaard-Bakken Recital Hall (Studio A) contains a Dobson three-manual tracker organ and is used for studio sessions, musical instruction, and rehearsals.

properties.NAME: Skoglund Athletic Center and Auditorium
properties.Information:
Skoglund Center hosts varsity basketball and volleyball games in its 2008-seat arena, and its natatorium is home to the swimming and diving teams.

  • Men's Basketball
  • Women's Basketball
  • Volleyball

    • Skoglund also has a field house, racquetball courts, wrestling room, locker rooms, an athletic training room, and is home to the Kinesiology Department. Outdoor tennis courts are located behind the building, near the softball, baseball and soccer fields.

    In addition to housing athletics, Skoglund Center is used for large ensemble performances - including the annual St. Olaf Christmas Festival.

properties.NAME: STOGROW Farm
properties.Information:
STOGROW, the on-campus farm of approximately 1.5 acres, is an entirely student-run community initiative. Each winter, a number of students are hired to work on the farm during the following summer and throughout the growing season, in addition to taking a course in the spring centered around sustainable farming practices. Students are able to directly apply lessons about agriculture that they have learned during their course, while also making decisions about what works best for them as they progress. STOGROW provides a place for students to practice and troubleshoot farming, learn from mistakes, and focus on improvement without worrying too much about the bottom line.

properties.NAME: Theater Building
properties.Information:
Formerly the women's gymnasium and once serving as the chapel, the Theater Building is home to the Theater Department.

The building contains two major performance spaces: Kelsey Theater, named in honor of Elizabeth Walsingham Kelsey, who was director of dramatics for more than three decades; and the smaller Haugen Theater, named in honor of former Professor of Theater Ralph A. Haugen.

properties.NAME: Thorson Hall
properties.Information: Thorson Halll houses 235 students and offers a spacious back yard with a patio and provides a striking view of the Northfield community. It has several features, most notably its spacious lounge that is a favorite study and conversation spot.

properties.NAME: Tom Porter Hall
properties.Information:
Part of the Ade Christenson Complex, Tom Porter Hall contains classrooms, offices, locker rooms, and athletic training room, and a weight room used by the variety football, track and field, and hockey teams. The facility is named after St. Olaf football coach Tom Porter '51.

properties.NAME: Tostrud Center
properties.Information:
Boasting an aerobics training facility, exercise machines, a weight-training facility, an elevated walking and jogging ring, a six-land 200 meter track, up to four volleyball or basketball courts, five indoor tennis courts, and a 48-foot high rock-climbing wall - the 95,000 square foot Tostrud Center is a state-of-the-art recreation and fitness center.

properties.NAME: Townhouses
properties.Information: The Townhouses are located along St. Olaf Ave on lower campus. 14 townhouses allow 140 St. Olaf Students the opportunity to enjoy apartment style living on a college campus. With centralized living room and kitchen spaces, students can easily foster a close-knit community.

properties.NAME: Ytterboe Hall
properties.Information: Ytterboe Hall houses 402 students in suites of four to ten residents. Each suite (or pod) consists of single and double rooms arranged around a common living area. This hall features a beautiful main lounge, study lounges, computer facilities, sinks in the rooms, and music practice rooms.
